description:
## Destination

Implement the ELK Layered layout engine in Beadsmith Graph Mode and make it the production default. The current app still renders the graph with the Dagre adapter, so the user cannot see any difference from the ELK spike. Preserve Dagre as a deterministic fallback and comparison baseline, but production Graph Mode must exercise ELK by default.

This issue is intentionally self-contained. The prior decision-quality spike is committed in the graph worktree and documented at `docs/research/elk-graph-layout-spike.md`; read that document and inspect the current code before changing anything. The spike issue was `bsm-1zl.10`.

## Why this work exists

Graph Mode currently lays out parent relationships first with Dagre and routes blocker relationships afterward with React Flow smooth-step paths. Because Dagre never sees blocker edges, it cannot minimize blocker crossings, reserve whitespace, or avoid unrelated Issue cards. The user screenshot showed red blocker paths running through cards and merging with other relationships. Path-style tuning alone cannot solve that structural problem.

The spike compared both engines on a deterministic 11-node fixture containing two parent trees, disconnected components, cross-tree blockers, sibling blockers, a closed blocker, a blocker cycle, a duplicate blocker declaration, and one missing endpoint. Observed diagnostics:

| Diagnostic | Dagre baseline | ELK with both edge classes |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Node overlaps | 0 | 0 |
| Edge-through-node pairs | 5 | 0 |
| Segment crossings | 3 | 1 |
| Duplicate edge IDs | 0 | 0 |
| Missing endpoints | 1 | 1 |
| Blocker cycles detected | 1 | 1 |
| Connected components | 3 | 3 |

ELK materially improves the routing evidence, but it also lets blocker relationships influence positions. This issue is the deliberate follow-up that turns that spike result into a user-visible production change.

## Existing spike assets

- `src/issues/issue-graph-layout.ts` already contains the extracted Dagre adapter, ELK conversion, explicit port definitions, ELK edge-section preservation, and geometry diagnostics. Reuse and deepen this seam instead of putting ELK JSON or Dagre policy back into `IssueGraphCanvas.tsx`.
- `src/issues/issue-graph-layout-fixture.ts` is the comparison fixture.
- `src/issues/issue-graph-layout.test.ts` proves explicit ports, orthogonal sections, deterministic Dagre behavior, blocker cycles, disconnected components, missing endpoints, and the hierarchy-only dead end.
- `scripts/render-elk-graph-spike.ts` regenerates the comparison artifact.
- `docs/research/elk-graph-layout-spike.svg` is the side-by-side baseline artifact.
- `docs/research/elk-graph-layout-spike.md` contains the recommendation, measurements, option names, and primary references.

## Required production behavior

1. Use ELK Layered for the rendered Graph Mode by default. There must be a real code path from `IssueGraphCanvas` to `layoutIssueGraphWithElk`; leaving ELK only in tests or the SVG script does not satisfy this issue.
2. Keep the semantic projection unchanged. Explicit `parent` remains authoritative; do not infer hierarchy from dotted IDs. Blocker edges remain derived only from each blocked Issue `blockedBy` field. Missing endpoints remain structured anomalies and must not create placeholder cards.
3. Keep the two relationship classes distinct. Use explicit ports: parent target north, parent source south, blocker target west, blocker source east. Preserve ELK edge sections or convert them into React Flow paths without throwing away the route and reconstructing the old generic smooth-step path.
4. Keep ELK asynchronous and safe for React rendering. On initial layout, show a clear layout-loading state. During recomputation, keep the last valid layout visible where possible. If ELK fails, surface a visible layout error and retain the graph data; use the Dagre adapter as a safe fallback if that is the chosen failure policy. Do not blank the Issue graph on layout failure.
5. Preserve current React Flow behavior: read-only nodes, pan and zoom, fit view, parent/blocker legend, card handles, Issue navigation, focused/all scope behavior, refresh behavior, and anomaly warnings.
6. Make the ELK layout stable enough for normal refreshes. Avoid unnecessary layout churn when the semantic graph is unchanged. If ELK output ordering needs a deterministic tie-breaker, use the existing sorted graph projection and the spike options rather than deriving new domain order from IDs.
7. Keep the current Dagre adapter available for fallback, diagnostics, and rollback. Do not delete `@dagrejs/dagre` in this issue.

## Important API findings and dead ends

- The tested dependency is `elkjs` 0.12.0. The ELK graph uses `elk.algorithm=layered`, downward direction, `elk.edgeRouting=ORTHOGONAL`, fixed port order, crossing minimization, connected-component separation, and explicit edge/node spacing. Use the exact options already documented in the spike rather than guessing new names.
- `elkjs/lib/elk-api.js` cannot be constructed without both `workerUrl` and `workerFactory`. The spike uses the browser bundle via a dynamic import for a no-worker path. If production moves to a Web Worker, configure it deliberately and test the asset path in the built Tauri app. Do not switch imports casually and discover this only at runtime.
- ELK Layered can break blocker cycles and return a finite layout, but the blocker cycle remains a domain diagnostic. Do not reject the graph, recurse indefinitely, or mutate the semantic projection to make the cycle disappear.
- Strategy B was tested and rejected as a routing solution: ELK laying out only parent edges returns only parent routes, not blocker routes. The official elkjs discussion indicates Layered routing is coupled to the Layered layout; do not simulate a routing-only mode with hidden nodes unless a new, measured design explicitly justifies that complexity.
- The current epic contract said parent links determine layout and blockers never influence positions. Production ELK with both edge classes intentionally relaxes that constraint. Keep parent hierarchy legible, document the contract change in the appropriate project docs/ADR if required, and do not silently preserve the old invariant while claiming ELK is active.
- The spike measured approximately 6.7 ms for the current Dagre adapter and 0.06 ms of ELK Layered execution time on the 11-node fixture. These measurements do not justify a worker by themselves. Use a worker only if the real focused-graph size or Tauri renderer responsiveness demonstrates a need.

## Tests and evidence

Add or update focused tests for:

- the production adapter selection proving Graph Mode invokes ELK by default;
- ELK node positions and routed sections reaching React Flow handles;
- no node overlap and no edge-through-card cases on the screenshot-shaped fixture;
- parent/blocker cycles, disconnected components, duplicate blocker declarations, and missing endpoints;
- async loading, last-valid-layout retention, and visible layout failure/fallback behavior;
- deterministic output or a documented tolerance for ELK output where exact coordinates are not stable.

Add a real desktop WebDriver scenario or equivalent reproducible built-app check that opens Graph Mode with a fixture containing cross-tree blockers and captures/asserts the visible graph. The checked-in SVG is useful evidence but is not a substitute for verifying the actual Tauri/React Flow renderer after wiring ELK into production.

Run the canonical gate; do not replace it with raw package commands:

```sh
mise run verify
```

Regenerate and inspect the visual comparison artifact as useful, but update it if the production route representation changes.

## Out of scope

- Relationship editing, manual arrangement, saved layouts, viewport persistence, search, Show all, Graph Issue Detail, reference navigation, backend/Rust/TauRPC changes, or a graph database.
- Adding a user-facing engine toggle unless implementation safety requires one. ELK should be the default behavior for this issue.
- Deleting Dagre or claiming success based only on the fixture-level adapter tests.

## Completion checklist

- [ ] ELK is the default production Graph Mode engine.
- [ ] React Flow renders the ELK route sections and keeps parent/blocker handles distinct.
- [ ] Loading, recomputation, failure, and fallback behavior are visible and preserve graph data.
- [ ] Semantic graph projection and engine-specific layout remain separate.
- [ ] Existing navigation, refresh, anomaly, scope, and read-only behavior remain intact.
- [ ] Real built desktop Graph Mode is visually checked with cross-tree blockers.
- [ ] Focused tests and the full `mise run verify` gate pass.
- [ ] The implementation explains any worker decision and updates the project documentation for the relaxed layout contract.

## Handoff

Start from a dedicated worktree. Run `bw prime`, then `bw start <this-issue-id>`. Inspect the spike files and current Graph Mode implementation before editing. Commit with this issue ID, close the issue, and run `bw sync`.
title: Adopt ELK Layered layout in Graph Mode
